title: Edit gallery feed descriptions
description:
The chronicle-reports feed is being added to Connect's set of **default** gallery feeds (posit-dev/connect#41144), and I think it would make sense to slightly tweak the category description and the descriptions of the two dashboard apps, to be more helpful to the user.  

- Category description: We can reword it to better match the descriptions of what the examples and extensions are.
- Chronicle Connect Dashboard description: We can reword it to better match the other published examples and extensions.  
- Chronicle Workbench Dashboard description: We can reword it to better match the other published examples and extensions. We should also include a line that references that this dashboard will not have data if you don't have Workbench. (Since there's no way to detect whether or not someone has Workbench, this app will automatically show for all Connect users, including those who do not have Workbench, so we would want to make it clear to them why the dashboard is empty if they add it).

pak::pak("posit-dev/chronicle-reports@dev")

title: `chronicle_data()` should fail gracefully when the curated directory does not exist
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When a Chronicle data root has not yet produced a particular curated dataset (for example, on a new install where the agent hasn't completed its first full collection-and-curation cycle, or where Connect data isn't being collected), `chronicle::chronicle_data()` calls `arrow::open_dataset()` directly on a path that doesn't exist. Arrow's filesystem layer raises:

`IOError: Cannot list directory '/var/lib/posit-chronicle/data/curated/v2/connect/user_totals/'. Detail: [errno 2] No such file or directory`

The Shiny app catches this in a `tryCatch` and logs `Error loading user totals: <message>` to stderr (see `inst/apps/connect/app.R:2520-2521`), then renders `NULL`. The dashboard surfaces this to operators as an opaque red error block at the page level.

In practice, operators see the raw Arrow error string and don't have enough context to know whether:

1. The Chronicle Agent isn't collecting Connect data at all,
2. Data hasn't yet aged through the ~30-hour refinement pipeline,
3. The `base_path` is pointing at the wrong location, or
4. The dataset simply doesn't exist for their deployment (e.g. Workbench-only install).

**Describe the solution you'd like**

In `R/utils.R` (the `chronicle_data()` helper), check that the directory exists before calling `arrow::open_dataset()`. If it does not, return `NULL` along with a one-line classified message that distinguishes "dataset never produced" from a real Arrow error. Callers in `inst/apps/connect/app.R` and `inst/apps/workbench/app.R` can then render a friendly placeholder (for example: "No `connect/user_totals` data has been curated yet — confirm that the Chronicle Agent has a valid `[Connect] APIKey` and that data has aged at least 30 hours since the agent began collecting.") instead of bubbling the raw Arrow exception.

Pseudocode for `chronicle_data()`:

```
chronicle_data <- function(metric, base_path = ...) {
  path <- chronicle_path(metric, base_path)
  if (!dir.exists(path)) {
    return(structure(NULL, class = "chronicle_missing_dataset", path = path, metric = metric))
  }
  arrow::open_dataset(path, hive_style = TRUE, partitioning = "date", format = "parquet")
}
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Doing the `dir.exists()` check inside each Shiny reactive: works but duplicates the same code across ~30 reactives in the two dashboards.
- Pre-creating empty curated directories at Chronicle Server startup: handled in a separate chronicle-server issue; this would still be useful as a defense-in-depth on the reports side.
- Improving the docs so operators know to expect the error: doesn't help the on-call who hits the error in production.

**Additional context**

Internal ref: ZD-128615.

The same defect class was previously fixed in the old cookbook code (in the `chronicle` repo) — see rstudio/chronicle#1274, "Report fails if data is missing" (closed 2024-08-26), whose error message was identical: `IOError: Cannot list directory '...' Detail: [errno 2] No such file or directory`. When reporting moved to this dedicated package, the `dir.exists()` guard wasn't carried forward.

Related file:line citations (current `main`):

- `R/utils.R:151-163` (chronicle_data)
- `inst/apps/connect/app.R:2506-2525` (the reactive that surfaces the error)
- `R/run_app.R:43-46`, `R/chronicle_constants.R:4` (base_path resolution)

title: Improve reports performance for large data sets
description:
## Related PRs
- https://github.com/posit-dev/chronicle-reports/pull/96
- https://github.com/posit-dev/chronicle-reports/pull/97

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

We have seen long load times for the reports internally here at Posit for our large dataset.  This can take up to 30 seconds to load the report in some cases.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Possible ways to improve this:
- Lazy load data so you can see the first report faster
- Find improvements in how we load things or how it is processed

title: Add details in README on how best to use Posit Assistant
description:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

As we think more about people building out their own reports, it would be good to ensure it's easy for people to use AI tools to build out or alter existing reports.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

There's a lot of great info already in the README on how to use the reports. But I think it would still be helpful to have guided details on using Positron along with Posit Assistant and/or Databot. Writing and trying these out may cause some additional changes, if we realize we need more docs in different places for instance.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

The alternative is just not to do this- people will likely figure this out themselves.

title: Add CSV downloads of data
description:
PR: https://github.com/posit-dev/chronicle-reports/pull/106
Deployed: https://connect.posit.it/connect/#/apps/e83d62f1-0a09-4055-b039-1bfc0cd8ec48

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

We've heard from one user that they would like to be able to download the data in CSV format, and there is likely more interest in this.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A button next to each graph and list which lets you download the data being displayed in CSV form.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

We could not have this in the reports, have it be some kind of API or documented thing for others to script out.  But this feels like the best way to go for users.

**Additional context**

I've done a Claude Code version of this which appears to work, although I don't pretend to know if all of the code makes sense.  I'll attach in a comment soon.

title: Sample data does not include all columns from production data
description:
## Related PRs
- https://github.com/posit-dev/chronicle-reports/pull/74

**Describe the bug**
Sample data generated from `chronicle_sample_data()` does not contain all of the columns present in the actual curated data sets generated by Chronicle Server.  

**System Details**

Chronicle Server Version: 2026.01.0

**To Reproduce**

```
# list columns in production data
names(chronicle_data("connect/user_totals"))
```
```
[1] "named_users"         "active_users_30days" "active_users_1day"   "administrators"      "publishers"          "viewers"             "licensed_user_seats" "date" 
```

```
# generate sample data and list columns
sample_path <- chronicle.reports::chronicle_sample_data()
names(chronicle_data("connect/user_totals", base_path = sample_path))
```

```
[1] "named_users"       "active_users_1day" "publishers"        "date"         
```

**Expected behavior**
Sample data columns should match production data.  

**Actual behavior**
A clear and concise description of what actually happened.

**Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

**Additional context**
I have not checked other tables to determine if they also are out of sync.  Probably should look at them all to be sure.  


**Testing Instructions**
Check each curated dataset on sample data and real data:
```
  names(chronicle_data("connect/user_totals"))
  names(chronicle_data("connect/content_list"))
  names(chronicle_data("connect/content_totals"))
  names(chronicle_data("connect/shiny_usage_totals_by_user"))
  names(chronicle_data("connect/content_visits_totals_by_user"))
  names(chronicle_data("connect/user_list"))
  names(chronicle_data("workbench/user_list"))
  names(chronicle_data("workbench/user_totals"))
```
